Rules of the road

Pinellas Trail E-Bike Rules, Stretch by Stretch

Speed limits, e-bike classes, sidewalks and helmets from St. Pete to Tarpon Springs, with the source for every answer.

By Tim Street · Last checked October 28, 2026
Before you ride: This is a plain-language summary, not legal advice. Rules change, sometimes without much notice. Check with the agency that manages the stretch you're riding, and obey any posted signs, before you ride.

Florida lets every agency that runs a path write its own e-bike rules, which is how a single ride on the Pinellas Trail can cross more than one set of them. The trail itself follows one set of county rules from end to end. The differences show up when you step off it: onto a city sidewalk, a waterfront path or a downtown street on the way to lunch. This page covers both, and every answer links to where it came from. Where an answer rests on a news report instead of an official rule page, we say so.

The short version

Speed limit
20 mph on the trail, or lower where posted
E-bike classes
Class 1, 2 and 3 allowed
Helmets
Required under 16
Sidewalks
Usually allowed; walk your bike in downtown Tarpon Springs
Trail hours
7 a.m. to sunset
Managed by
Pinellas County Parks & Conservation Resources, (727) 582-2100, option 2

Ask about your ride

Type a question about the stretch you're riding. Answers come only from the rules on this page, with the source and the date we last checked it. If we don't have the answer, it will tell you who to call instead of guessing.

Common questions

What is the speed limit on the Pinellas Trail?

20 mph, according to the Pinellas County Sheriff's Office. The county's own trail rules say riders must obey the posted speed limit, so if a sign on your stretch shows something lower, the sign is the rule. That 20 mph applies to every e-bike class, including Class 3 bikes that can assist up to 28 mph.

Source: City of Dunedin · Pinellas County. Checked October 28, 2026.

Which e-bike classes are allowed on the Pinellas Trail?

All three. The county's trail guide treats Class 1 (pedal assist to 20 mph), Class 2 (throttle to 20 mph) and Class 3 (pedal assist to 28 mph) as bicycles, and the trail's ban on motorized vehicles makes an exception for e-bikes. A Class 3 is legal on the trail, but you can't use its top speed range because the trail limit is 20 mph.

Source: Pinellas County · City of Dunedin. Checked October 28, 2026.

Can I use a throttle (Class 2) e-bike on the trail?

Yes. The county's trail guide lists Class 2, throttle-on-demand bikes that cut off at 20 mph, among the e-bikes treated as bicycles on the trail.

Source: Pinellas County. Checked October 28, 2026.

What makes a bike too powerful for the trail?

Under Florida law an e-bike has working pedals, a seat, two or three wheels and a motor of 750 watts or less. The Sheriff's Office says a legal e-bike tops out at 28 mph under power and has no illegal modifications. A bike that fails any of those tests is treated as a motor vehicle that needs registration and a licensed driver, and it isn't allowed on the trail. If your bike has been 'unlocked' or had its controller swapped, it may no longer qualify.

Source: The Florida Senate · City of Dunedin. Checked October 28, 2026.

Are electric trikes allowed on the Pinellas Trail?

A three-wheeled e-trike that meets the rest of Florida's e-bike definition (working pedals, a seat, a motor of 750 watts or less) is an e-bike under state law, so the same trail rules apply to it. Keep in mind the county asks riders not to take up more than half the trail.

Source: The Florida Senate · Pinellas County. Checked October 28, 2026.

Can I ride my e-bike on the sidewalk in Pinellas County?

Usually, but not everywhere. Florida law lets you ride a bicycle, including an e-bike, on a sidewalk, where you have the rights and duties of a pedestrian: you must yield to people on foot and give an audible warning before passing them. Cities and counties can restrict e-bikes on sidewalks, and any ordinance that allows them must cap speeds at 15 mph. Pinellas County has not adopted a countywide sidewalk rule. St. Petersburg allows bikes on sidewalks except where signs say otherwise. Tarpon Springs now requires you to walk any bike through its busiest downtown sidewalks. When you leave the trail, watch for signs.

Source: The Florida Senate · The Florida Senate · Tampa Bay Beacons · City of St. Petersburg · Bay News 9. Checked October 28, 2026. Partly from news reports
The state-law and St. Petersburg parts come from official pages. The county's decision and the Tarpon Springs rule come from news reports.

Are the rules different on the trail than on a sidewalk?

Yes. On the trail, the county's rules apply: 20 mph, keep right, pass on the left and warn before passing. On a sidewalk, state law treats you like a pedestrian, so people on foot always have the right of way and any local speed cap can't be more than 15 mph. Some city sidewalks, like parts of downtown Tarpon Springs, are walk-your-bike zones.

Source: Pinellas County · City of Dunedin · The Florida Senate · The Florida Senate · Bay News 9. Checked October 28, 2026. Partly from news reports
The Tarpon Springs walk-zone detail comes from news reports.

Do I have to wear a helmet on the Pinellas Trail?

Only riders and passengers under 16 are required to wear one, under Florida law and the county's trail rules. Adults aren't required to, though it's a good idea.

Source: The Florida Senate · Pinellas County. Checked October 28, 2026.

Do I need a license, registration or ID to ride an e-bike?

No license, registration or insurance is needed for a legal e-bike in Florida. Since 2025, state law has allowed local governments to require riders to carry a government-issued photo ID. Pinellas County has not adopted that rule. Local news has reported that some Pinellas cities have adopted restrictions allowed under the law, without naming them, so carrying your driver's license is a cheap safeguard.

Source: The Florida Senate · Tampa Bay Beacons. Checked October 28, 2026. Partly from news reports
The state-law part comes from the statute. What Pinellas cities have adopted comes from news reports.

Is there a minimum age to ride an e-bike on the trail?

Not on the Pinellas Trail as of our last check. State law lets local governments set minimum ages, and county commissioners discussed it in 2026, but the county decided in October 2026 to wait for the Legislature before writing any new e-bike rules.

Source: The Florida Senate · WUSF · Tampa Bay Beacons. Checked October 28, 2026. Partly from news reports
The state-law part comes from the statute. The county's October 2026 decision comes from news reports.

What are the Pinellas Trail's hours? Can I ride after dark?

The county lists the trail as open daily from 7 a.m. to sunset. Anywhere you ride between sunset and sunrise, Florida law requires a white front light visible from 500 feet plus a red rear light and a red reflector.

Source: Pinellas County · The Florida Senate. Checked October 28, 2026.

What are the basic trail etiquette rules?

Keep right and pass on the left. Warn people before you pass, with a bell or by saying 'on your left.' Don't stop or stand on the trail; step off to rest. Groups shouldn't take up more than half the trail, and dogs must be on a leash no longer than 6 feet.

Source: Pinellas County · Pinellas County. Checked October 28, 2026.

Are the Pinellas e-bike rules about to change?

Possibly, but not right away. Gov. DeSantis vetoed the statewide e-bike safety bill (SB 382) in June 2026. Pinellas County commissioners decided in October 2026 to wait for the 2027 legislative session before writing their own rules, and Forward Pinellas is working with county staff on proposals. St. Petersburg council members have also talked about a city ordinance. We'll update this page when anything is adopted.

Source: Tampa Bay Beacons · Tampa Bay Beacons · WUSF. Checked October 28, 2026. Partly from news reports

Stretch by stretch

Here's what changes, and what doesn't, from the south end of the trail to the north.

Downtown St. Petersburg and the North Bay Trail connection

The southern trailhead at First Avenue Southeast and Bayshore Drive, where the Pinellas Trail meets the city's North Bay Trail along the waterfront.

Speed
Pinellas Trail: 20 mph. North Bay Trail (city): St. Petersburg posted 10 mph signs in August 2026 and limited riders to under 15 mph; police have said they're focusing on warnings first.
E-bike classes
Class 1, 2 and 3 on the Pinellas Trail.
Sidewalks
St. Petersburg allows bikes on sidewalks except where signs prohibit it. Ride at a walking-friendly pace and yield to pedestrians.
Helmets
Required under 16.
Who to ask
Pinellas County Parks & Conservation Resources, (727) 582-2100, option 2; City of St. Petersburg, (727) 893-7111

The 10 mph North Bay Trail limit comes from news reports, not a city ordinance we could read. If you're riding the waterfront, go by the posted signs.

Source: Pinellas County · City of Dunedin · Tampa Bay Beacons · City of St. Petersburg · Florida Rambler. Checked October 28, 2026. Partly from news reports

St. Petersburg to Clearwater (Gulfport, South Pasadena, Seminole, Largo, Belleair, Clearwater)

The long middle stretch of the trail.

Speed
20 mph, or lower where posted.
E-bike classes
Class 1, 2 and 3.
Sidewalks
No countywide sidewalk restriction. We haven't found a city along this stretch with its own e-bike sidewalk rule; obey any posted signs.
Helmets
Required under 16.
Who to ask
Pinellas County Parks & Conservation Resources, (727) 582-2100, option 2

Expect frequent road crossings. Stop at stop signs and don't assume you have the right of way at major roads like State Road 60 in Clearwater.

Source: Pinellas County · City of Dunedin · Pinellas County · Tampa Bay Beacons. Checked October 28, 2026.
The 'no countywide rule' point comes from news coverage of the county's October 2026 decision.

Downtown Dunedin

The trail runs straight through downtown and serves as its main walkway, with shops and restaurants facing it.

Speed
20 mph, but downtown is crowded and the county says fast riding is inappropriate in busy areas. Plan on going much slower here.
E-bike classes
Class 1, 2 and 3.
Sidewalks
We haven't found a Dunedin rule restricting e-bikes on downtown sidewalks as of our last check.
Helmets
Required under 16.
Who to ask
Pinellas County Parks & Conservation Resources, (727) 582-2100, option 2

Slow down or stop where the trail crosses Main Street.

Source: Pinellas County · City of Dunedin · Pinellas County · Florida Rambler. Checked October 28, 2026.

Palm Harbor

The unincorporated stretch between Dunedin and Tarpon Springs.

Speed
20 mph, or lower where posted.
E-bike classes
Class 1, 2 and 3.
Sidewalks
No countywide sidewalk restriction.
Helmets
Required under 16.
Who to ask
Pinellas County Parks & Conservation Resources, (727) 582-2100, option 2

Palm Harbor isn't a city, so county rules are the only local rules here.

Source: Pinellas County · City of Dunedin · Tampa Bay Beacons. Checked October 28, 2026.
The 'no countywide rule' point comes from news coverage of the county's October 2026 decision.

Tarpon Springs, including side trips downtown and to the Sponge Docks

The northern end of the trail, and the short detours riders take into downtown and to the Sponge Docks for lunch.

Speed
Trail: 20 mph. Off the trail, state law caps speeds on sidewalks at 15 mph where local rules allow e-bikes.
E-bike classes
Class 1, 2 and 3 on the trail.
Sidewalks
Walk your bike, any bike, on the sidewalks of East Tarpon Avenue between Pinellas Avenue and Ring Street, Dodecanese Boulevard between Pinellas Avenue and Roosevelt Boulevard, and in Craig Park. The city can add temporary walk zones during big events such as First Friday and Hippie Fest. Fines start with a warning or up to $50, then $100 for a second offense and $250 for a third.
Helmets
Required under 16.
Who to ask
Pinellas County Parks & Conservation Resources, (727) 582-2100, option 2; City of Tarpon Springs

Tarpon Springs passed this rule in September 2026, according to news reports; signs were going up that fall. The rule covers sidewalks, not the Pinellas Trail itself. We couldn't find the ordinance text on the city's website, so check the posted signs or call the city.

Source: Pinellas County · Bay News 9 · Tampa Bay Beacons · The Florida Senate · Florida Rambler. Checked October 28, 2026. Partly from news reports

What this page doesn't cover

  • The Duke Energy Trail and the eastern half of the Pinellas Trail Loop
  • Beaches and the beach towns
  • Trails outside Pinellas County, such as the Suncoast Trail or the Withlacoochee State Trail
  • Electric scooters, e-motos and other devices that aren't legal e-bikes, except to explain why they aren't allowed

Who to call

  • Pinellas County Parks & Conservation Resources, (727) 582-2100, option 2. Manages and maintains the Pinellas Trail.
  • Pinellas County Sheriff's Office. Enforces trail rules; city police also enforce inside their city limits.
  • Pinellas County Information Desk, (727) 464-3000. General county questions, weekdays 8 a.m. to 5 p.m..
  • City of St. Petersburg, (727) 893-7111. City streets, sidewalks and the North Bay Trail.
  • City of Tarpon Springs. Downtown and Sponge Docks sidewalks.
